# Adjudication Task — Chapter 233

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃233화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|중년인은 투명한 검신을 물끄러미 내려다봤다.
  6|
  7|칼날 같은 이목구비와 굳게 다물어진 입술. 드문드문 흰 터럭이 섞이기 시작한 머리가 검신에 비쳤다.
  8|
  9|그가 문득 입을 연 것은 잠시 후였다.
 10|
 11|“기다리느라 고생 많았네.”
 12|
 13|나직하지만 힘 있는 목소리가 넓은 방 내부를 울린다. 그러나 눈이 닿는 곳 어디에도 사람은 없었다.
 14|
 15|대답이 들려온 것은 중년인의 머리 위, 천장이었다.
 16|
 17|“제 소임입니다.”
 18|
 19|속삭이는 목소리의 주인공은 비선(秘線)이라 불리는 인물이었다. 전대에도, 전 전대에도. 가문이 처음 세워진 수백 년 전부터 비선은 존재했다.
 20|
 21|오직 한 사람, 가주에게 절대적인 충성을 맹세한 그들은 비선이라는 이름 그대로 숨겨진 실이었다.
 22|
 23|그 실을 따라 흘러들어온 수많은 정보는 조용히 잊힐 수도, 누군가의 목을 조르는 무기가 될 수도 있었다.
 24|
 25|“그래, 새로운 소식이 있나?”
 26|
 27|“예. 천(天)급입니다.”
 28|
 29|“천급이라.”
 30|
 31|중년인의 손가락이 검신을 쓸었다.
 32|
 33|지금까지 비선이 전해 준 소식은 하나같이 기밀이지만 그 경중에 따라 천, 지, 인으로 나뉘었다.
 34|
 35|천급은 그중에서도 가장 높다.
 36|
 37|벌써 이십 년 가까이 가문을 이끌고 있는 중년인으로서도 결코 흔히 겪는 일이 아니었다.
 38|
 39|“오랜만이로군. 황산파 이후 처음인가?”
 40|
 41|황산파는 장구한 역사를 지닌 명문 대파다. 그러나 이제는 세인들의 기억 속에서 서서히 잊혀 가는 이름이기도 했다.
 42|
 43|적자생존.
 44|
 45|무림은 도태된 자들을 돌아보지 않는 냉혹한 세상이다. 중년인은 황산파를 도태시켰고 그들의 시체를 뜯어먹었다.
 46|
 47|“봉문이 풀리기까지는 한참 남았을 터인데.”
 48|
 49|“황산파는 이미 와해되었습니다. 봉문이 풀리더라도 회복 불능입니다.”
 50|
 51|“하면?”
 52|
 53|“산주(山主)가 돌아왔습니다.”
 54|
 55|짤막한 대답에 검신을 어루만지던 손끝이 우뚝 멈췄다.
 56|
 57|“……그게 사실인가?”
 58|
 59|“틀림없습니다.”
 60|
 61|산주, 산의 주인.
 62|
 63|누군가는 그 무슨 뜬구름 잡는 소리냐며 고개를 갸웃할지 모른다. 천하에 산이 몇 개인데 주인을 따지냐며 경을 칠 수도 있다.
 64|
 65|그러나 이곳, 안휘성에서 산의 주인은 단 한 사람을 가리키는 단어였다.
 66|
 67|“화왕 적천강…….”
 68|
 69|단신으로 천 명의 무인을 대적한 미증유의 고수.
 70|
 71|구화산은 그의 영역이었고 수백 년간 계승된 열화문의 성지였다.
 72|
 73|마교도들이 구화산에 불을 지른 그 날, 평범하게 늙어 가던 한 노인은 화왕이 되었다.
 74|
 75|덕분에 소중한 보금자리를 지켜 낸 안휘성 사람들은 경의를 담아 그를 산주라 부르기 시작했다.
 76|
 77|“언제, 어디서 들어온 소식인가?”
 78|
 79|“두 시진 전 북문을 통과했다는 보고입니다.”
 80|
 81|“목적지는?”
 82|
 83|“구화산입니다.”
 84|
 85|“그렇군.”
 86|
 87|작게 고개를 끄덕이던 중년인은 문득 이상함을 느꼈다.
 88|
 89|가주 자리에 오른 뒤부터 지금까지, 비선으로부터 수많은 보고를 받고 의견을 물었지만 단 한 번도 단언한 적이 없던 그다.
 90|
 91|그러나 이번에는 달랐다.
 92|
 93|주군의 의문을 느낀 비선이 먼저 입을 열었다.
 94|
 95|“제자와 동행했습니다. 사문으로 가는 것은 당연하지요.”
 96|
 97|“제자?”
 98|
 99|중년인이 눈살을 찌푸렸다. 열화문은 일인전승의 문파. 화왕의 제자라면 한 사람밖에 없지 않은가.
100|
101|근 이십 년 전의 일이지만 그는 화왕과 관련된 일은 똑똑히 기억하고 있었다.
102|
103|“혹 그 잔악한 놈을 다시 찾아온 건가?”
104|
105|“생각하시는 사람은 아닙니다. 확인된 바에 의하면 그는 석 달 전 죽었습니다.”
106|
107|“그리고 새로운 제자를 찾았다?”
108|
109|“예.”
110|
111|비선의 고저 없는 목소리가 이어졌다.
112|
113|“진태경, 올해 스물하나가 되었고 태원진가의 직계입니다.”
114|
115|“이름도, 가문도 처음 듣는 것 같은데.”
116|
117|“정마대전에서 활약했던 화양검, 그리고 최근 십봉룡이라 불리며 두각을 드러내고 있는 진천검과 같은 핏줄입니다.”
118|
119|“아, 바로 그 진가로군.”
120|
121|“예.”
122|
123|다행히 비선의 입에서 흘러나온 두 개의 이름은 중년인에게도 제법 귀에 익었다.
124|
125|“흠, 그렇단 말이지.”
126|
127|중년인은 비선의 존재도 잊은 채 골똘히 생각에 잠겼다.
128|
129|태원진가의 진태경. 화왕 적천강의 새로운 제자. 아무리 생각해도 낯선 이름. 하지만 이제는 익숙해져야 했다.
130|
131|‘변방 무가의 핏줄이 화왕에게 선택받았다.’
132|
133|약관이 넘은 청년을 새로운 제자로 받아들였다는 것은 모종의 이유가 있지 않고서야 불가능한 일이다.
134|
135|‘둘 중 하나겠지. 화왕의 약점을 잡았거나, 나이와 출신 따위는 상관없을 정도로 극히 뛰어난 무재를 갖고 있거나.’
136|
137|생각이 이어질수록 가닥이 잡혀 갔다.
138|
139|상념에 빠져 있던 중년인이 다시 입을 열었을 때는 이미 상당한 시간이 흐른 뒤였다.
140|
141|“소선(小線)을 모두 움직이게.”
142|
143|소선이란 비선의 밑에서 움직이는 무수한 정보원들이었다.
144|
145|천하 각지에서 정보를 전해오는 그들은 비선을 거쳐 중년인에게 흘러 들어간다.
146|
147|“모두 말입니까?”
148|
149|되묻는 비선의 목소리에는 지금까지와는 달리 희미한 놀라움이 배어 있었다.
150|
151|중년인의 명령은 가문의 정보력 중 태반을 한 사람에게 쏟아붓겠다는 뜻이었으니까.
152|
153|그러나 놀라움도 잠시뿐, 자신의 본분을 깨달은 비선이 황급히 대답했다.
154|
155|“결례를 저질렀습니다.”
156|
157|“상관없네. 달포를 줄 테니 무슨 수를 써서라도 그 제자에 관한 모든 걸 알아 오게.”
158|
159|“존명.”
160|
161|“당분간 바빠질걸세.”
162|
163|그 말에 숨겨진 말뜻을 알아차린 비선의 기척이 씻은 듯이 사라졌다.
164|
165|절정의 끝에 다다른 은형술(隱形術). 그는 앞으로 보름간 눈코 뜰 새 없는 시간을 보낼 것이다.
166|
167|‘나도 놀고 있을 수만은 없지.’
168|
169|중년인은 천천히 자리에서 일어났다.
170|
171|뼛속까지 무인이었던 아버지와는 달리 그는 지도자의 피를 타고났다.
172|
173|소가주 시절부터 가문을 이끌며 패자(霸者)의 위치를 공고히 다져 온 중년인의 전신에서는 위엄이 흘러넘쳤다.
174|
175|저벅, 저벅, 저벅.
176|
177|큰 걸음으로 넓은 공간을 가로지른 중년인이 문을 활짝 열어젖혔다. 전각을 둘러싼 십여 명의 호위들이 한쪽 무릎을 꿇으며 그를 맞이했다.
178|
179|“가주를 뵙습니다!”
180|
181|중년인은 작게 고개를 끄덕였다. 그들 한 사람, 한 사람이 뛰어난 절정 검수이며 같은 피를 이은 혈족이었다.
182|
183|남궁(南宮)이라는 성씨 아래 모인 거대한 집단, 천하 무림에 뿌리내린 거목.
184|
185|“식솔들을 소집하거라. 날이 좋으니 함께 술이라도 한잔해야겠구나.”
186|
187|“존명!”
188|
189|중년인, 남궁룡은 고개를 들어 하늘을 바라보았다.
190|
191|구름 한 점 없는, 끝없이 펼쳐진 창천(蒼天)이 그곳에 있었다.
192|
193|
194|
195|* * *
196|
197|
198|
199|나는 세상에서 가장 진지한 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
200|
201|“제게는 오랫동안 간직해 온 소원이 하나 있습니다.”
202|
203|적천강도 진중한 목소리로 대답했다.
204|
205|“노부도 소원이 하나 있다.”
206|
207|“실례가 안 된다면 제가 먼저 말해도 될까요?”
208|
209|“충분히 실례다.”
210|
211|“그럼 이번 한 번만 실례를 저지르겠습니다.”
212|
213|“바지에 실례하고 싶으냐? 이번 한 번이 아니라 평생 똥오줌 질질 싸게 해 줘?”
214|
215|“……아.”
216|
217|우리 엄마가 이 광경을 봤으면 억장이 무너졌을 거다.
218|
219|서러워서 눈물이 날 것 같았지만 꾹 참고 다시 입을 열었다.
220|
221|“한 번만 들어 주세요.”
222|
223|“오냐, 네놈 속이야 뻔하지만 한 번은 들어 주마.”
224|
225|마른침을 꼴깍 삼킨 내가 소원을 말했다.
226|
227|“객잔 한 번만 들르면 안 될까요?”
228|
229|“그게 소원이냐?”
230|
231|“예.”
232|
233|“그럼 노부의 소원도 말하마.”
234|
235|적천강이 무시무시한 눈빛으로 나를 쏘아봤다.
236|
237|“주둥이 닥치고 따라와라.”
238|
239|“……아니, 왜요?”
240|
241|“수련하고 싶다며? 수련하러 가는데 뭐가 그렇게 쫑알쫑알 불만이 많으냐?”
242|
243|“제가 언제 안 한다고 했습니까? 앞으로 반년이나 산에 처박혀 있을 거니까 그 전에 한 번만, 딱 한 번만 배불리 먹고 씻자는 거죠!”
244|
245|어둠이 드리워진 산속에 내 외침이 쩌렁쩌렁 울려 퍼졌다.
246|
247|맞다. 지금 우리가 서 있는 이곳은 안휘성에 위치한 구화산의 초입이다.
248|
249|“산서성에서 하남까지 칠 주야! 하남에서 안휘까지 또 칠 주야 걸렸습니다. 그간 잠도 제대로 못 잤어요.”
250|
251|그나마 하남에 도착하기 전까지는 잠이라도 한 시진씩 재워 줬었는데, 굉도의 거처를 나온 후에는 말 그대로 얄짤 없었다.
252|
253|식사 시간도 없이 육포를 씹으며 뛰고, 또 뛰었다.
254|
255|“소림사 산채비빔밥 먹고 싶었는데!”
256|
257|보름간의 강행군 동안 제대로 된 식사라고는 낙양의 객잔에서 했던 것이 유일하다.
258|
259|“그마저도 노야 혼자서 다리 다 먹고! 날개 한 짝에 퍽퍽살만 남겨 두고!”
260|
261|이제 겨우 고기 몇 점 뜯어 먹나 했더니, 웬 흑도 칼잡이 놈들이 튀어나와 훼방을 놓고 언더아머 스님이 나타나서 소림사로 데려가더라.
262|
263|“객잔 한 번 가자고 그렇게 말씀드렸더니 노야께서 뭐라고 하셨습니까? 거의 다 왔다고. 가서 쉬자고 하셨잖아요!”
264|
265|“그래서 다 왔잖아. 구화산.”
266|
267|때가 낀 새끼손톱으로 귀를 후비적거린 적천강이 귓밥을 훅 불었다.
268|
269|“가서 쉬어. 올라가면 배불리 먹고 씻고 잘 수 있다.”
270|
271|“배불리 먹어 봤자 육포, 벽곡단이잖아요. 뜨거운 물은 고사하고 산림욕만 실컷 하고, 잠은 하루에 반 시진도 안 재워 줄 거면서!”
272|
273|“으허허!”
274|
275|껄껄 웃던 적천강이 웃음을 뚝 그쳤다. 동시에 스산한 기운이 그의 전신에서 흘러나왔다.
276|
277|“이래서 감이 좋은 아해는 마음에 안 든다니까.”
278|
279|“……!”
280|
281|에드 오빠……가 아니라, 등골을 타고 소름이 쭉 돋는다.
282|
283|얼음처럼 차가운 목소리가 그의 입에서 뱉어져 나왔다.
284|
285|“그래, 네 녀석의 짐작이 맞다. 하루 반 시진씩 재우며 개같이 굴릴 생각이다.”
286|
287|“헉.”
288|
289|“벽곡단으로 몸에 낀 기름을 한 방울도 남기지 않고 쥐어짠 다음, 반년간 하루도 빠짐없이 인간이 상상할 수 있는 최대치의 수련을 시켜 주마.”
290|
291|“아, 악마.”
292|
293|“노부에게 마귀라고 한 것이냐? 수련 강도를 더 높여야겠군.”
294|
295|“아, 안 돼. 이건 사기야.”
296|
297|“알아차렸을 때는 이미 늦었다는 걸 왜 모르느냐?”
298|
299|“잠시만요. 저 잠깐 측간 좀 다녀올게요.”
300|
301|슬금슬금 뒷걸음치는 나를 향해 화왕이 주름진 손바닥이 펼쳤다.
302|
303|“올 때는 마음대로지만 갈 때는 아니란다.”
304|

The middle-aged man nodded slightly, then sensed something odd.

[P44]
Since becoming Family Head, he had received countless reports from the Hidden Thread and asked for his assessments, but the man had never once spoken with such certainty.

[P45]
This time was different.

[P46]
Sensing his lord’s doubt, the Hidden Thread spoke first.

[P47]
“He was accompanied by his Disciple. It is only natural that he would return to his sect.”

[P48]
“His Disciple?”

[P49]
The middle-aged man frowned. The Fire Gate Clan passed its teachings from one master to a single Disciple. The Fire King could have only one.

[P50]
Though it had happened nearly twenty years ago, he clearly remembered everything concerning the Fire King.

[P51]
“Did he take back that vicious bastard?”

[P52]
“It is not the man you are thinking of. According to confirmed reports, he died three months ago.”

[P53]
“And the Fire King found a new Disciple?”

[P54]
“Yes.”

[P55]
The Hidden Thread’s flat voice continued.

[P56]
“Jin Taekyung. He turned twenty-one this year and belongs to the direct line of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P57]
“Both the name and the family are unfamiliar to me.”

[P58]
“He shares a bloodline with the Blade of Flowers, who distinguished himself during the Great Faction War, and the Heaven Shaking Sword, who has recently risen to prominence as one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”

[P59]
“Ah, that Jin Family.”

[P60]
“Yes.”

[P61]
Fortunately, the two names given by the Hidden Thread were familiar enough to the middle-aged man.

[P62]
“Hmm. So that is how it is.”

[P63]
He sank into thought, forgetting even the Hidden Thread’s presence.

[P64]
Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s new Disciple. No matter how much he considered it, the name remained unfamiliar.

[P65]
But it was one he would have to remember from now on.

[P66]
*The Fire King chose a descendant of a frontier martial family.*

[P67]
He would never have accepted a man already past twenty as his new Disciple without good reason.

[P68]
*It must be one of two things. Either he has some leverage over the Fire King, or his martial talent is so extraordinary that his age and background are irrelevant.*

[P69]
The longer he considered it, the clearer the answer became.

[P70]
A considerable amount of time had passed by the time he spoke again.

[P71]
“Set every Lesser Thread in motion.”

[P72]
The Lesser Threads were the countless informants serving beneath the Hidden Thread.

[P73]
They gathered information from all across the realm, which flowed through the Hidden Thread before reaching the middle-aged man.

[P74]
“Every one of them?”

[P75]
For the first time, a faint trace of surprise entered the Hidden Thread’s voice.

[P76]
The order meant focusing most of the family’s intelligence network on a single person.

[P77]
But his surprise lasted only a moment. Remembering his duty, the Hidden Thread quickly answered.

[P78]
“Forgive my insolence.”

[P79]
“It doesn’t matter. I’ll give you a month. Use whatever means necessary and learn everything there is to know about that Disciple.”

[P80]
“As you command.”

[P81]
“You’ll be busy for a while.”

[P82]
The Hidden Thread grasped the meaning behind those words, and his presence vanished as though it had been wiped clean.

[P83]
His concealment technique had reached the very limits of the Peak realm. He would spend the next fortnight without a moment to breathe.

[P84]
*I can’t sit idle either.*

[P85]
The middle-aged man slowly rose.

[P86]
Unlike his father, who had been a martial artist to the bone, he had been born to lead.

[P87]
He had guided the family since his days as Lesser Family Head, cementing its position as a dominant power. Authority radiated from his entire bearing.

[P88]
Step. Step. Step.

[P89]
He crossed the spacious room in long strides and threw open the doors. The dozen or so guards surrounding the pavilion dropped to one knee in greeting.

[P90]
“We greet the Family Head!”

[P91]
The middle-aged man nodded slightly. Every one of them was an outstanding Peak swordsman and a blood relative who shared his lineage.

[P92]
They were a vast clan united beneath the surname Namgung—a great tree rooted deep in the Murim.

[P93]
“Gather the clan. The weather is fine, so we should all share a drink.”

[P94]
“As you command!”

[P95]
The middle-aged man, Namgung Ryong, raised his head toward the sky.

[P96]
The boundless azure heaven stretched above him, not a single cloud in sight.

[P97]
* * *

[P98]
I spoke with the most solemn expression I could muster.

[P99]
“I have a wish I’ve cherished for a long time.”

[P100]
Jeok Cheongang answered in an equally grave voice.

[P101]
“This old man has a wish as well.”

[P102]
“If it wouldn’t be too rude, may I go first?”

[P103]
“That would be extremely rude.”

[P104]
“Then I’ll be rude just this once.”

[P105]
“Want to have an accident in your pants? Should I make you piss and shit yourself for the rest of your life, not just this once?”

[P106]
“…”

[P107]
My mother would have been devastated if she had seen this.

[P108]
I could have cried at how unfair it was, but I held back my tears and tried again.

[P109]
“Please, just hear me out.”

[P110]
“Fine. I know exactly what you’re after, but I’ll hear you out once.”

[P111]
I swallowed dryly and stated my wish.

[P112]
“Could we stop at an inn just once?”

[P113]
“That’s your wish?”

[P114]
“Yes.”

[P115]
“Then this old man will tell you his.”

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with terrifying eyes.

[P117]
“Shut your mouth and follow me.”

[P118]
“…Why?”

[P119]
“Didn’t you say you wanted to train? We’re on our way to train, so what are you whining about?”

[P120]
“When did I say I didn’t want to? I’m going to be stuck in the mountains for the next six months. All I’m asking is that we eat our fill and wash up once—just once—before that!”

[P121]
My shout echoed through the darkened mountains.

[P122]
That was right. We were standing at the foot of Mount Jiuhua in Anhui Province.

[P123]
“It took seven days and nights to get from Shanxi Province to Henan, then another seven days and nights to get from Henan to Anhui. I haven’t even slept properly.”

[P124]
At least before we reached Henan, he had let me sleep for a shichen at a time. After we left Hong Dao’s residence, however, he had shown me absolutely no mercy.

[P125]
We ran and ran, chewing jerky without even stopping for meals.

[P126]
“I wanted to eat Shaolin Temple’s wild-vegetable bibimbap!”

[P127]
During the fifteen-day forced march, the only proper meal I’d had was at the inn in Luoyang.

[P128]
“And even then, you ate all the drumsticks! You left me one wing and nothing but dry breast meat!”

[P129]
I had barely managed to tear off a few pieces when a bunch of sword-wielding dark-path figures showed up and ruined everything. Then the Under Armour monk appeared and dragged me off to Shaolin Temple.

[P130]
“I kept asking you to stop at an inn. What did you say? That we were almost there. That we could rest when we arrived!”

[P131]
“And here we are. Mount Jiuhua.”

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang dug into his ear with a grimy pinky nail, then blew the earwax away.

[P133]
“Go up and rest. Once we’re there, you can eat your fill, wash, and sleep.”

[P134]
“Eating my fill just means jerky and fasting pills. Forget hot water—I’ll get nothing but a nonstop forest bath. And you won’t even let me sleep for half a shichen a day!”

[P135]
“Hahaha!”

[P136]
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then stopped dead. At the same time, a chilling energy seeped from his entire body.

[P137]
“This is why I don’t like youngsters with sharp instincts.”

[P138]
“…!”

[P139]
*Big Brother Ed…*

[P140]
Wait, no.

[P141]
Goose bumps raced down my spine.

[P142]
His voice came out cold as ice.

[P143]
“Yes, you guessed correctly. I intend to let you sleep for half a shichen a day and work you like a dog.”

[P144]
I sucked in a breath.

[P145]
“I’ll use fasting pills to squeeze every last drop of fat from your body. Then, for six months straight, I’ll put you through the most extreme training humanly imaginable, without missing a single day.”

[P146]
“Y-you devil.”

[P147]
“Did you just call this old man a demon? I suppose I’ll have to make your training even harder.”

[P148]
“N-no. This is a scam.”

[P149]
“Why don’t you understand that by the time you realize that, it’s already too late?”

[P150]
“Wait. I need to visit the privy for a moment.”

[P151]
As I slowly backed away, the Fire King extended a wrinkled palm toward me.

[P152]
“You came of your own free will, but leaving isn’t up to you.”

[P153]
Whoosh!

[P154]
An overwhelming force I had never felt before became ropes that bound my entire body.

[P155]
Neither my near-superhuman physical abilities nor my nearly one jiazi[^2] of internal energy could do a thing.

[P156]
I tried to resist, but it was already too late. With a flick of his hand, my body rose into the air.

[P157]
“Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?”

[P158]
“If you recognize it, hurry over.”

[P159]
Whoosh!

[P160]
The next moment, I shot toward Jeok Cheongang faster than an arrow. At the same time, one of his wrinkled fingers brushed a spot on my neck.

[P161]
A sharp sting was followed by an ominous sound in my ear.

[P162]
Beep!

[P163]
> **System**
>
> You have been struck by **Pressure-Point Strike**!
>
> Your **Sleep Acupoint** has been struck. You cannot resist sleep!
>
> 5 seconds, 4 seconds, 3 seconds, 2 seconds…

[P164]
Drowsiness swept over me with the System’s countdown.

[P165]
As my consciousness blurred, Jeok Cheongang’s voice slowly receded into the distance.

[P166]
“Today, I’ll make a special exception and let you sleep for two shichen.”

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
*Well, fuck. How very generous.*

[P169]
I couldn’t force the words from the tip of my tongue before sleep claimed me.

[P170]
* * *

[P171]
Snore. Snore.

[P172]
“That young bastard is absurdly strong.”

[P173]
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue as he looked at the sleeping Jin Taekyung.

[P174]
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space and Pressure-Point Strike were not omnipotent. The amount of force they required varied depending on the opponent.

[P175]
It was a good thing he had known what kind of monster the young man was. If he had let down his guard and allowed the technique to be countered, he would have thoroughly humiliated himself.

[P176]
“It feels like only yesterday that I met him in Shanxi, yet he has already come this far… What a strange fellow.”

[P177]
Just as Jeok Cheongang let out a weary sigh, his vision suddenly blurred and the strength drained from his legs.

[P178]
“Gasp!”

[P179]
His hand shot out and caught a nearby tree just in time.

[P180]
His heart pounded, and his mind snapped fully awake as though someone had dumped cold water over him in his sleep.

[P181]
“Th-this…”

[P182]
Had he expended too much strength at once? Or had his aged body failed to withstand the arduous journey?

[P183]
Jeok Cheongang bit his lip. His prime as a martial artist might have passed, but he was still a Supreme Peak master who had reached the summit of martial arts.

[P184]
It was not his flesh that had grown old, but something else.

[P185]
*I must hurry. I don’t have much time.*

[P186]
Perhaps that was why his old friend Hong Dao had told him to leave immediately.

[P187]
After steadying himself, Jeok Cheongang slung Jin Taekyung over his back. Though he was more than a hundred years old, the young man’s massive frame felt as light as a feather.

[P188]
“Not yet. It can’t happen yet.”

[P189]
He muttered in a voice that had suddenly grown much older, then set off.

[P190]
More than ten jang vanished beneath each step, and the scenery flashed past.

[P191]
Before long, thick fog rolled in and erased every trace of him.

[P192]
[^1]: A *shichen* is a traditional Chinese time unit of approximately two hours.

[P193]
[^2]: A *jiazi* is a traditional sixty-year cycle.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{

"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 233

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃233화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|중년인은 투명한 검신을 물끄러미 내려다봤다.
  6|
  7|칼날 같은 이목구비와 굳게 다물어진 입술. 드문드문 흰 터럭이 섞이기 시작한 머리가 검신에 비쳤다.
  8|
  9|그가 문득 입을 연 것은 잠시 후였다.
 10|
 11|“기다리느라 고생 많았네.”
 12|
 13|나직하지만 힘 있는 목소리가 넓은 방 내부를 울린다. 그러나 눈이 닿는 곳 어디에도 사람은 없었다.
 14|
 15|대답이 들려온 것은 중년인의 머리 위, 천장이었다.
 16|
 17|“제 소임입니다.”
 18|
 19|속삭이는 목소리의 주인공은 비선(秘線)이라 불리는 인물이었다. 전대에도, 전 전대에도. 가문이 처음 세워진 수백 년 전부터 비선은 존재했다.
 20|
 21|오직 한 사람, 가주에게 절대적인 충성을 맹세한 그들은 비선이라는 이름 그대로 숨겨진 실이었다.
 22|
 23|그 실을 따라 흘러들어온 수많은 정보는 조용히 잊힐 수도, 누군가의 목을 조르는 무기가 될 수도 있었다.
 24|
 25|“그래, 새로운 소식이 있나?”
 26|
 27|“예. 천(天)급입니다.”
 28|
 29|“천급이라.”
 30|
 31|중년인의 손가락이 검신을 쓸었다.
 32|
 33|지금까지 비선이 전해 준 소식은 하나같이 기밀이지만 그 경중에 따라 천, 지, 인으로 나뉘었다.
 34|
 35|천급은 그중에서도 가장 높다.
 36|
 37|벌써 이십 년 가까이 가문을 이끌고 있는 중년인으로서도 결코 흔히 겪는 일이 아니었다.
 38|
 39|“오랜만이로군. 황산파 이후 처음인가?”
 40|
 41|황산파는 장구한 역사를 지닌 명문 대파다. 그러나 이제는 세인들의 기억 속에서 서서히 잊혀 가는 이름이기도 했다.
 42|
 43|적자생존.
 44|
 45|무림은 도태된 자들을 돌아보지 않는 냉혹한 세상이다. 중년인은 황산파를 도태시켰고 그들의 시체를 뜯어먹었다.
 46|
 47|“봉문이 풀리기까지는 한참 남았을 터인데.”
 48|
 49|“황산파는 이미 와해되었습니다. 봉문이 풀리더라도 회복 불능입니다.”
 50|
 51|“하면?”
 52|

“Want to have an accident in your pants? Should I make you piss and shit yourself for the rest of your life, not just this once?”

[P106]
“…”

[P107]
My mother would have been devastated if she had seen this.

[P108]
I could have cried at how unfair it was, but I held back my tears and tried again.

[P109]
“Please, just hear me out.”

[P110]
“Fine. I know exactly what you’re after, but I’ll hear you out once.”

[P111]
I swallowed dryly and stated my wish.

[P112]
“Could we stop at an inn just once?”

[P113]
“That’s your wish?”

[P114]
“Yes.”

[P115]
“Then this old man will tell you his.”

[P116]
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with terrifying eyes.

[P117]
“Shut your mouth and follow me.”

[P118]
“…Why?”

[P119]
“Didn’t you say you wanted to train? We’re on our way to train, so what are you whining about?”

[P120]
“When did I say I didn’t want to? I’m going to be stuck in the mountains for the next six months. All I’m asking is that we eat our fill and wash up once—just once—before that!”

[P121]
My shout echoed through the darkened mountains.

[P122]
That was right. We were standing at the foot of Mount Jiuhua in Anhui Province.

[P123]
“It took seven days and nights to get from Shanxi Province to Henan, then another seven days and nights to get from Henan to Anhui. I haven’t even slept properly.”

[P124]
At least before we reached Henan, he had let me sleep for a shichen at a time. After we left Hong Dao’s residence, however, he had shown me absolutely no mercy.

[P125]
We ran and ran, chewing jerky without even stopping for meals.

[P126]
“I wanted to eat Shaolin Temple’s wild-vegetable bibimbap!”

[P127]
During the fifteen-day forced march, the only proper meal I’d had was at the inn in Luoyang.

[P128]
“And even then, you ate all the drumsticks! You left me one wing and nothing but dry breast meat!”

[P129]
I had barely managed to tear off a few pieces when a bunch of sword-wielding dark-path figures showed up and ruined everything. Then the Under Armour monk appeared and dragged me off to Shaolin Temple.

[P130]
“I kept asking you to stop at an inn. What did you say? That we were almost there. That we could rest when we arrived!”

[P131]
“And here we are. Mount Jiuhua.”

[P132]
Jeok Cheongang dug into his ear with a grimy pinky nail, then blew the earwax away.

[P133]
“Go up and rest. Once we’re there, you can eat your fill, wash, and sleep.”

[P134]
“Eating my fill just means jerky and fasting pills. Forget hot water—I’ll get nothing but a nonstop forest bath. And you won’t even let me sleep for half a shichen a day!”

[P135]
“Hahaha!”

[P136]
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then stopped dead. At the same time, a chilling energy seeped from his entire body.

[P137]
“This is why I don’t like youngsters with sharp instincts.”

[P138]
“…!”

[P139]
*Big Brother Ed…*

[P140]
Wait, no.

[P141]
Goose bumps raced down my spine.

[P142]
His voice came out cold as ice.

[P143]
“Yes, you guessed correctly. I intend to let you sleep for half a shichen a day and work you like a dog.”

[P144]
I sucked in a breath.

[P145]
“I’ll use fasting pills to squeeze every last drop of fat from your body. Then, for six months straight, I’ll put you through the most extreme training humanly imaginable, without missing a single day.”

[P146]
“Y-you devil.”

[P147]
“Did you just call this old man a demon? I suppose I’ll have to make your training even harder.”

[P148]
“N-no. This is a scam.”

[P149]
“Why don’t you understand that by the time you realize that, it’s already too late?”

[P150]
“Wait. I need to visit the privy for a moment.”

[P151]
As I slowly backed away, the Fire King extended a wrinkled palm toward me.

[P152]
“You came of your own free will, but leaving isn’t up to you.”

[P153]
Whoosh!

[P154]
An overwhelming force I had never felt before became ropes that bound my entire body.

[P155]
Neither my near-superhuman physical abilities nor my nearly one jiazi[^2] of internal energy could do a thing.

[P156]
I tried to resist, but it was already too late. With a flick of his hand, my body rose into the air.

[P157]
“Seizing an Object Through Empty Space?”

[P158]
“If you recognize it, hurry over.”

[P159]
Whoosh!

[P160]
The next moment, I shot toward Jeok Cheongang faster than an arrow. At the same time, one of his wrinkled fingers brushed a spot on my neck.

[P161]
A sharp sting was followed by an ominous sound in my ear.

[P162]
Beep!

[P163]
> **System**
>
> You have been struck by **Pressure-Point Strike**!
>
> Your **Sleep Acupoint** has been struck. You cannot resist sleep!
>
> 5 seconds, 4 seconds, 3 seconds, 2 seconds…

[P164]
Drowsiness swept over me with the System’s countdown.

[P165]
As my consciousness blurred, Jeok Cheongang’s voice slowly receded into the distance.

[P166]
“Today, I’ll make a special exception and let you sleep for two shichen.”

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
*Well, fuck. How very generous.*

[P169]
I couldn’t force the words from the tip of my tongue before sleep claimed me.

[P170]
* * *

[P171]
Snore. Snore.

[P172]
“That young bastard is absurdly strong.”

[P173]
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue as he looked at the sleeping Jin Taekyung.

[P174]
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space and Pressure-Point Strike were not omnipotent. The amount of force they required varied depending on the opponent.

[P175]
It was a good thing he had known what kind of monster the young man was. If he had let down his guard and allowed the technique to be countered, he would have thoroughly humiliated himself.

[P176]
“It feels like only yesterday that I met him in Shanxi, yet he has already come this far… What a strange fellow.”

[P177]
Just as Jeok Cheongang let out a weary sigh, his vision suddenly blurred and the strength drained from his legs.

[P178]
“Gasp!”

[P179]
His hand shot out and caught a nearby tree just in time.

[P180]
His heart pounded, and his mind snapped fully awake as though someone had dumped cold water over him in his sleep.

[P181]
“Th-this…”

[P182]
Had he expended too much strength at once? Or had his aged body failed to withstand the arduous journey?

[P183]
Jeok Cheongang bit his lip. His prime as a martial artist might have passed, but he was still a Supreme Peak master who had reached the summit of martial arts.

[P184]
It was not his flesh that had grown old, but something else.

[P185]
*I must hurry. I don’t have much time.*

[P186]
Perhaps that was why his old friend Hong Dao had told him to leave immediately.

[P187]
After steadying himself, Jeok Cheongang slung Jin Taekyung over his back. Though he was more than a hundred years old, the young man’s massive frame felt as light as a feather.

[P188]
“Not yet. It can’t happen yet.”

[P189]
He muttered in a voice that had suddenly grown much older, then set off.

[P190]
More than ten jang vanished beneath each step, and the scenery flashed past.

[P191]
Before long, thick fog rolled in and erased every trace of him.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
